**D.** The pedestrian won't prevail, because the adjuster was an adverse party with no fiduciary duty to protect the pedestrian's interests. That means the pedestrian couldn't justifiably rely on his statement about the law. My earlier answer, C, isn't one of the two options the team note allows. The pedestrian also suffered no loss from the statement, since he rejected the offer and won $550,000, so the claim fails on damages either way.

CONFIDENCE: 62
